review_basis: The current engine/src/retail/core/native_0048f970.cpp (sha256 35213d3e...) and its header (sha256 03da6f73...) were read line by line. The retail body 0x0048F970-0x0048FA71 was disassembled and decompiled with the active Binary Ninja PE view; its CFG was recovered independently with radare2 afbj and angr CFGFast. candidate_semantics.calling_convention: stdcall (retl $0x10 in the shared epilogue at 0x0041FA29), four dword stack arguments
candidate_semantics.chain_walk: Same order as retail: head handler first, then advance to head->next and repeat while that node's next is non-null. Two additional guards: chain head != null (0x41F99C) and caller->handler != null (0x41F9DF).
candidate_semantics.dispatch: cmp message,0x1C: je WM_ACTIVATEAPP, jbe low path. High path: 0x0104 then 0x0105 else default. Low path: 0x0001 then 0x0002 else default. The same constant partition as retail; the two disjoint sub-tests are emitted in the opposite lexical order but cannot both match, so the dispatch mapping is unchanged.
candidate_semantics.wm_destroy: clear byte [0x5D5C6C]; ShowCursor(1); PostQuitMessage(0); return 0. The retail 0x004010B0 call is omitted.
candidate_semantics.wm_syskeydown: VK_F4 (0x73): if [0x5D5C68] != 0, PostMessageA(g_window_handle, 2, 0, 0); else VK_MENU (0x12): [0x5D5C68] = 1; always return 0.
candidate_semantics.default: tail jmp through the DefWindowProcA import with the same four arguments; DefWindowProcA returns directly to the window caller.

divergences: Head-null guard (candidate 0x41F99C-0x41F9A4 tests [0x5D5C70] and branches to dispatch): retail 0x0048F989 loads [0x005C8DF0] and 0x0048F98E dereferences it with no null test. The retail initialiser at 0x0048F68C writes the sentinel cell 0x005C8DF4, so a valid chain head is normally non-null; this guard is unreachable under that invariant and is candidate-only.

Handler-null guard (candidate 0x41F9DF-0x41F9E4 tests [ecx+8] and branches to the dispatch): retail 0x0048F99C calls [eax+8] unconditionally. Registration writes the handler at +0x08 before insertion, so this guard is unreachable for a valid chain and is candidate-only.

The WM_DESTROY call to 0x004010B0 at retail 0x0048F9D4 has no candidate counterpart. The 28-byte body 0x004010B0-0x004010CB is unreconstructed, so the candidate omits it instead of faking a no-op. This is a real behavioral gap on WM_DESTROY, not a control-flow change: the surrounding clear/ShowCursor/PostQuitMessage order is preserved.
Retail returns from each branch through its own pop/ret sequence; the candidate jumps to one shared epilogue at 0x41FA18. Semantically equivalent.
Retail calls DefWindowProcA and then pops and executes ret 0x10; the candidate tail-jumps to the DefWindowProcA import (0x41FA68). Semantically equivalent for the return value and arguments.
Retail lowers the message dispatch with cmp/ja/je and dec chains; the candidate uses direct cmp/je/jbe chains. The constants and the resulting dispatch mapping are identical.

Retail WM_ACTIVATEAPP calls 0x00498460; the candidate calls the repository transcription FP_InitExtendedPrecision of that same native. The 0x00498460 static-analysis evidence records the same fnstcw/or 0x0C00/fldcw sequence and the same global control-word slot.

Retail calls the zero-argument getter 0x0048F0A0 at 0x0048FA45 and passes its result to PostMessageA; the candidate reads its own g_window_handle global directly. The 0x0048F0A0 analysis proves the getter is exactly one load of 0x005C8BC4, so the expression is equivalent provided the candidate global holds the same window handle at the call.

The candidate WindowHandlerEntry declares the previous link at +0x04 but LinkWindowHandler does not maintain it. WindowProcedure never reads +0x04, so this has no effect on the dispatch; it is recorded as a limitation of the ported chain, not of this function's control flow.
limitations: No paired retail/candidate runtime evidence exists. This review is static and structural; it does not prove behavioral equivalence, WM_ACTIVATEAPP activation semantics, or the WM_DESTROY side effects.
The WM_DESTROY 0x004010B0 call is omitted, so the candidate does not reproduce the complete retail WM_DESTROY side-effect sequence.

The two null guards add candidate-only branches whose outcome differs from retail only when the chain is malformed (retail would read/deref null or call a null handler; the candidate continues to message dispatch).

The candidate binary analyzed (4af8c894...) was built from source digest 3031bb9d... (candidate-receipt.json); the only later source changes are provenance/status comments, so the machine code is unchanged, but no rebuilt binary exists in this task scope.
The previous-link field of the chain node is not maintained by LinkWindowHandler.
The candidate has no paired runtime runner, so this record cannot rise above STRUCTURALLY_VERIFIED.

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja, radare2 and angr all identify a single retail function at 0x0048F970, 258 bytes, 21 radare2 blocks and 29 edges; the candidate binary exports _WindowProcedure@16 at 0x0041F970 with the same four-argument disassembly. The function identity and boundaries agree.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Both sides read four dword stack arguments in the order window, message, wParam, lParam. The candidate passes them to the chain callback in that order (push lParam, wParam, message, window), matching the retail push order and the cdecl handler cleanup (add esp,0x10).

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The compared constants are identical: 0x001C WM_ACTIVATEAPP, 0x0001, 0x0002 WM_DESTROY, 0x0104 WM_SYSKEYDOWN, 0x0105 WM_SYSKEYUP, 0x12 VK_MENU, 0x73 VK_F4, ShowCursor arg 1, PostQuitMessage arg 0, PostMessageA(hwnd, 2, 0, 0), and return 0. No scaling or arithmetic transformation is involved.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: The retail node stride is 12 bytes with next at +0x00 and handler at +0x08; the candidate struct is 12 bytes with handler at +0x08 (static_assert in the test harness and MinGW probe). The four retail globals map by role to the four candidate globals. The previous link at +0x04 is declared but not maintained, which does not affect this function's accesses.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: Every call the candidate makes corresponds to a retail call with the same arguments and order: ShowCursor(1), PostQuitMessage(0), PostMessageA(hwnd,2,0,0), DefWindowProcA(window,message,wParam,lParam), and the 0x00498460 chop-rounding native. The retail-only call to 0x004010B0 is a known omission listed in divergences; this check certifies the candidate's call sites, not the retail's complete side-effect set.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: Handled messages and a zero chain result return 0; the default path returns the DefWindowProcA result. The candidate's extra null guards send malformed-chain states to message dispatch instead of retail's fault, which is listed as a divergence rather than claimed as retail behavior.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: The only floating-point effect is the WM_ACTIVATEAPP branch. Retail 0x00498460 executes fwait; fnstcw word [0x006E5BC4]; or word [0x006E5BC4],0x0C00; fldcw word [0x006E5BC4]; ret, forcing x87 rounding control bits 10-11 to truncate. The candidate calls the repository transcription FP_InitExtendedPrecision of that native; the focused test checks the resulting control word is 0x0F7F on x86. This is statement/structural agreement, not runtime observation.
